I haven't written a methodology description, because **nothing in this system is built yet**, so there is no method to critique.

**What the repository contains**

- One commit ("initial commit").
- Four workspace packages: `sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download`, `sec-edgar-index-ingest` and `sec-edgar-ingest`. Each is a bare `uv init` scaffold:
  - an empty README and `py.typed`
  - an `__init__.py` holding only the `hello()` stub
  - a `pyproject.toml` with `dependencies = []` and the placeholder description
- The root `pyproject.toml` points a `sec-edgar` script at a `sec_edgar` module that doesn't exist.
- No tests, fixtures, config or infrastructure.
- `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md` is marked **PROPOSED (2026-10-05), pending design acceptance**. It states that every path in it is proposed and that no repository was inspected.

No outcome of the filing-index ingestion system (discovery, collection, parsing, reconciliation or publication) works end to end on real data. A description written now would be a paraphrase of the design spec, not of a working method. The reviewer would end up critiquing a proposal while believing it was an implemented system.

**Where this should go instead**

The right next step is **derive-roadmap's New-Project Entry**. Use the spec and `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md` as its inputs, so it can stage what to build first. Start a fresh session and say:

> "Use derive-roadmap (New-Project Entry) on specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, with specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md as background."

The spec's own §7 step 1 is "Accept the ADR and this spec". You may want to settle that acceptance before or during the roadmap work.

**After it's built**

Come back to describe-critique-methodology once at least one outcome runs end to end on real data. Good candidates are the parse → canonical catalog path with its identity and precedence rules (§4.4), or the reconciliation and withdrawal gate. Those are the methodologically interesting parts, and they would make a good module-level description for external critique.
